title: A Subgoal-driven RL Framework for Improving Long-Horizon Web Agents
claim: Decomposing a goal into subgoals that feed training and inference-time planning lifts a base agent's success rate beyond stronger baselines.
layout: Left-to-right flow with two routes (A, B) feeding stacked bar charts at right
description: The left side is a pipeline. A user icon and a goal box ("Find the nearest cafe within 50-mile range of CMU") feed a yellow "SGG: Subgoal Generator" module inside a dashed box labeled "Decomposing the goal to subgoals" (§5.1). A web environment panel (WebArena apps, OS icons) sits above and connects to the generator. The generator outputs a blue box listing subgoals in natural language, which goes to a yellow "Target Agents" box. Two routes lead from the subgoals: (A) Offline Reward Shaping + RLFT (§5.3) and (B) Online Planning during Inference Time (§5.2). Thick arrows from each route point to two bar charts on the right under the blue heading "Milestoning enhances the capability of the base model". The charts compare Gemma-12b, SFT and MiRA (43.0) on WebArena-Lite, and GPT-4o, GPT-4-Turbo, Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini-SGO (32.1). Ours is highlighted with blue hatching.
caption: Overview of the Milestoning the Agents
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents have emerged as powerful autonomous controllers for digital environments, spanning mobile interfaces, operating systems, and web browsers. Web navigation, for example, demands handling dynamic content and long action sequences, making it a particularly complex task. Existing LLM-backed agents exhibit weakened long-horizon planning abilities during RL fine-tuning, where sparse and delayed rewards from terminal Outcome Reward Models (ORMs) make it difficult for agents to identify the actions that lead to success, preventing them from sustaining coherent reasoning over extended tasks. We address this with two contributions: (1) a validated subgoal generation procedure that produces reliable, monotonically calibrated progress signals between the initial state and the terminal ORM reward; and (2) MiRA ($\underline{Mi}$lestoning your $\underline{R}$einforcement Learning Enhanced $\underline{A}$gent), an RL training framework using dense, milestone-based reward signals via a learned potential critic. Starting from the open Gemma3-12B base ($6.4$%), MiRA enables the agent to reach $43.0$% on the WebArena-Lite benchmark. This performance surpasses proprietary systems such as GPT-4-Turbo ($17.6$%) and GPT-4o ($13.9$%), as well as the previous open-model state of the art, WebRL ($38.8$%). Our findings demonstrate that milestone-based reward shaping significantly boosts an agent's long-horizon abilities, paving the way for more robust, general-purpose autonomous systems.
